records.choice: I paint a large red spiral on this object, clearly visible from across the platform.
records.caption: You paint a sweeping red spiral onto the wooden bench. It stands out starkly against the weathered timber, a bold new mark on the decaying platform, easily visible even from the far end of the harbor.

records.choice: I follow the road out of town toward Innsmouth.
records.caption: The bus, an ancient hulk, rattles and groans as it pulls away from the depot, leaving the salt-choked air and the distant cry of gulls behind. The road ahead, cracked and overgrown, winds into the gathering gloom. The town recedes in the rearview mirror, its gabled roofs and narrow lanes swallowed by the encroaching shadows.

travel.description: A desolate, overgrown road leading into the fog-shrouded, decaying town of Innsmouth. Weathered, gambrel-roofed houses line the distant streets, their windows dark and uninviting. The air grows heavy with the scent of salt and decay, and a low, distant hum seems to emanate from the sea.

records.choice: I go down the alley beside this road.
records.caption: You turn from the main road, leaving the gnarled trees and oppressive fog behind. The alley beside the house is narrower, darker, and the silence here feels heavier. The scent of brine intensifies, mixing with something vaguely organic and decaying.

records.choice: I walk through the depot doors into the depot interior.
records.caption: The heavy timber doors of the bus depot creak open as you push through, revealing the dimly lit interior. The salty air outside gives way to the stale, close atmosphere within, carrying faint echoes of distant gulls.

travel.description: The interior of the bus depot is cavernous and damp. Old, peeling advertisements for long-defunct shipping lines cling to the walls. The air is still and heavy, carrying the scent of dust, brine, and something faintly metallic. The bus from outside dominates the space, its rear door ajar, while a small, grimy counter serves as a ticket booth. Dim light filters in from high windows, barely illuminating the cobweb-draped corners.

records.choice: I walk through the doorway into the fog outside.
records.caption: You step through the doorway. The stale air of the depot is immediately replaced by the damp, chilling embrace of the Innsmouth fog. The world outside is a muted tapestry of grey, the familiar platform now barely visible through the swirling mist.
